sanskrit: ācāryaṃ ye ca te 'rakṣan duryodhanapurogamāḥ drauṇikarṇakṛpās tāta te 'py akurvan kim āhave
english: And those who guarded the teacher, with Duryodhana at their head — Aśvatthāman, Karṇa, and Kṛpa — what, my son, did they too do in the battle?

sanskrit: bhāradvājaṃ jighāṃsantau savyasācivṛkodarau samārchan māmakā yuddhe kathaṃ saṃjaya śaṃsa me
english: When Savyasācin and Vṛkodara sought to slay the son of Bharadvāja, how did my men close with them in the fight? Tell me, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: sindhurājavadheneme ghaṭotkacavadhena te amarṣitāḥ susaṃkruddhā raṇaṃ cakruḥ kathaṃ niśi
english: By the slaying of the king of the Sindhus and by the slaying of Ghaṭotkaca, these men were made furious and greatly enraged — how did they wage the battle in the night?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hate ghaṭotkace rājan karṇena niśi rākṣase praṇadatsu ca hṛṣṭeṣu tāvakeṣu yuyutsuṣu
english: Saṃjaya said: When the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca had been slain by Karṇa in the night, O king, and your men, eager for battle, were roaring in their delight,

sanskrit: āpatatsu ca vegena vadhyamāne bale 'pi ca vigāḍhāyāṃ rajanyāṃ ca rājā dainyaṃ paraṃ gataḥ
english: as they charged on with fury and the army was being cut down, deep in the night the king fell into the utmost wretchedness.

sanskrit: abravīc ca mahābāhur bhīmasenaṃ paraṃtapaḥ āvāraya mahābāho dhārtarāṣṭrasya vāhinīm haiḍimbasyābhighātena moho mām āviśan mahān
english: And the mighty-armed scorcher of foes said to Bhīmasena: "Hold back, O mighty-armed one, the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son; at the death of Haiḍimba's son a great stupor has come over me."

sanskrit: evaṃ bhīmaṃ samādiśya svarathe samupāviśat aśrupūrṇamukho rājā niḥśvasaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ kaśmalaṃ prāviśad ghoraṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇasya vikramam
english: Having so charged Bhīma, the king sat down upon his own chariot, his face filled with tears and sighing again and again; beholding Karṇa's prowess, he sank into a dreadful despondency.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā vyathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇo vacanam abravīt mā vyathāṃ kuru kaunteya naitat tvayy upapadyate vaiklavyaṃ bharataśreṣṭha yathā prākṛtapūruṣe
english: Seeing him so stricken, Kṛṣṇa spoke these words: "Grieve not, son of Kuntī; such faltering does not befit you, O best of the Bharatas, as it would a common man."

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha rājan yudhyasva vaha gurvīṃ dhuraṃ vibho tvayi vaiklavyam āpanne saṃśayo vijaye bhavet
english: "Rise, O king, fight, bear the heavy yoke, O lord; should faltering overtake you, victory itself would fall into doubt."

sanskrit: śrutvā kṛṣṇasya vacanaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vimṛjya netre pāṇibhyāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing Kṛṣṇa's words, the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira wiped his eyes with both hands and spoke to Kṛṣṇa:

sanskrit: viditā te mahābāho dharmāṇāṃ paramā gatiḥ brahmahatyāphalaṃ tasya yaḥ kṛtaṃ nāvabudhyate
english: "Known to you, O mighty-armed one, is the highest course of all duties; the guilt of slaying a brahmin belongs to him who does not recognize a kindness done to him."

sanskrit: asmākaṃ hi vanasthānāṃ haiḍimbena mahātmanā bālenāpi satā tena kṛtaṃ sāhyaṃ janārdana
english: "For when we dwelt in the forest, the great-souled son of Hiḍimbā, though still but a boy, rendered us his aid, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: astrahetor gataṃ jñātvā pāṇḍavaṃ śvetavāhanam asau kṛṣṇa maheṣvāsaḥ kāmyake mām upasthitaḥ uṣitaś ca sahāsmābhir yāvan nāsīd dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "When he learned that the white-steeded Pāṇḍava had gone in quest of weapons, that mighty archer, O Kṛṣṇa, attended upon me in the Kāmyaka forest, and dwelt with us all the while Dhanaṃjaya was absent."

sanskrit: gandhamādanayātrāyāṃ durgebhyaś ca sma tāritāḥ pāñcālī ca pariśrāntā pṛṣṭhenoḍhā mahātmanā
english: "On the journey to Gandhamādana we were carried across the hard passes by him, and the weary Pāñcālī was borne upon the back of that great-souled one."

sanskrit: ārambhāc caiva yuddhānāṃ yad eṣa kṛtavān prabho madarthaṃ duṣkaraṃ karma kṛtaṃ tena mahātmanā
english: "And from the very outset of the battles, whatever this one performed — a hard task accomplished for my sake by that great-souled one, O lord —"

sanskrit: svabhāvād yā ca me prītiḥ sahadeve janārdana saiva me dviguṇā prītī rākṣasendre ghaṭotkace
english: "and the love I bear by nature for Sahadeva, O Janārdana — even that love, doubled, I bore for Ghaṭotkaca, lord of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: bhaktaś ca me mahābāhuḥ priyo 'syāhaṃ priyaś ca me yena vindāmi vārṣṇeya kaśmalaṃ śokatāpitaḥ
english: "Devoted to me was that mighty-armed one, and I was dear to him, and he was dear to me — and through him, O Vārṣṇeya, I am sunk in despair, tormented by grief."

sanskrit: paśya sainyāni vārṣṇeya drāvyamāṇāni kauravaiḥ droṇakarṇau ca saṃyattau paśya yuddhe mahārathau
english: "Look, O Vārṣṇeya, at the armies being driven in rout by the Kauravas; look at Droṇa and Karṇa, those great chariot-warriors, locked in the fight."

sanskrit: niśīthe pāṇḍavaṃ sainyam ābhyāṃ paśya pramarditam gajābhyām iva mattābhyāṃ yathā naḍavanaṃ mahat
english: "At dead of night behold the Pāṇḍava army crushed by these two, as a great thicket of reeds is trampled by two rutting elephants."

sanskrit: anādṛtya balaṃ bāhvor bhīmasenasya mādhava citrāstratāṃ ca pārthasya vikramante sma kauravāḥ
english: "Heedless of the strength of Bhīmasena's arms, O Mādhava, and of the varied weaponry of Pārtha, the Kauravas press on in their might."

sanskrit: eṣa droṇaś ca karṇaś ca rājā caiva suyodhanaḥ nihatya rākṣasaṃ yuddhe hṛṣṭā nardanti saṃyuge
english: "Here are Droṇa and Karṇa, and king Suyodhana too, having slain the rākṣasa in battle, roaring in their joy upon the field."

sanskrit: katham asmāsu jīvatsu tvayi caiva janārdana haiḍimbaḥ prāptavān mṛtyuṃ sūtaputreṇa saṃgataḥ
english: "How, while we yet live, and you too, O Janārdana, has Haiḍimba met his death, fallen upon by the son of the sūta?"

sanskrit: kadarthīkṛtya naḥ sarvān paśyataḥ savyasācinaḥ nihato rākṣasaḥ kṛṣṇa bhaimasenir mahābalaḥ
english: "Setting us all at naught, before the very eyes of Savyasācin, the mighty rākṣasa, Bhīmasena's son, has been slain, O Kṛṣṇa."

sanskrit: yadābhimanyur nihato dhārtarāṣṭrair durātmabhiḥ nāsīt tatra raṇe kṛṣṇa savyasācī mahārathaḥ
english: "When Abhimanyu was slain by the evil-souled sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the great chariot-warrior Savyasācin was not there in that battle, O Kṛṣṇa."

sanskrit: niruddhāś ca vayaṃ sarve saindhavena durātmanā nimittam abhavad droṇaḥ saputras tatra karmaṇi
english: "And we were all held off by the evil-souled lord of the Sindhus; Droṇa, together with his son, was the instrument in that deed."

sanskrit: upadiṣṭo vadhopāyaḥ karṇasya guruṇā svayam vyāyacchataś ca khaḍgena dvidhā khaḍgaṃ cakāra ha
english: "The means of the slaying was taught to Karṇa by the teacher himself, who cut in two with his sword the sword of the struggling boy."

sanskrit: vyasane vartamānasya kṛtavarmā nṛśaṃsavat aśvāñ jaghāna sahasā tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī tathetare maheṣvāsāḥ saubhadraṃ yudhy apātayan
english: "As he stood in his distress, Kṛtavarman, like one without pity, suddenly slew his horses and both his rear-guard charioteers; thus did the other mighty archers bring down the son of Subhadrā in the fight."

sanskrit: alpe ca kāraṇe kṛṣṇa hato gāṇḍīvadhanvanā saindhavo yādavaśreṣṭha tac ca nātipriyaṃ mama
english: "And for but a slight cause, O Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the Sindhus was slain by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, O best of the Yādavas — and even that is not greatly to my liking."

sanskrit: yadi śatruvadhe nyāyyo bhavet kartuṃ ca pāṇḍavaiḥ droṇakarṇau raṇe pūrvaṃ hantavyāv iti me matiḥ
english: "If the slaying of an enemy were proper and to be done by the Pāṇḍavas, then it was Droṇa and Karṇa who should first have been slain in battle — such is my judgment."

sanskrit: etau mūlaṃ hi duḥkhānām asmākaṃ puruṣarṣabha etau raṇe samāsādya parāśvastaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: "For these two are the root of our sorrows, O bull among men; relying upon these two in battle, Suyodhana is filled with confidence."

sanskrit: yatra vadhyo bhaved droṇaḥ sūtaputraś ca sānugaḥ tatrāvadhīn mahābāhuḥ saindhavaṃ dūravāsinam
english: "Where Droṇa ought to have been slain, and the sūta's son with his followers, there the mighty-armed one slew instead the far-dwelling lord of the Sindhus."

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā kāryaḥ sūtaputrasya nigrahaḥ tato yāsyāmy ahaṃ vīra svayaṃ karṇajighāṃsayā bhīmaseno mahābāhur droṇānīkena saṃgataḥ
english: "Yet without fail the subduing of the sūta's son must be wrought by me; therefore I shall go myself, O hero, in my desire to slay Karṇa, while the mighty-armed Bhīmasena is engaged with Droṇa's host."

sanskrit: evam uktvā yayau tūrṇaṃ tvaramāṇo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sa visphārya mahac cāpaṃ śaṅkhaṃ pradhmāpya bhairavam
english: Having spoken thus, Yudhiṣṭhira hastened swiftly forth, twanging his great bow and blowing a fearsome blast upon his conch.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṇa gajānāṃ ca śatais tribhiḥ vājibhiḥ pañcasāhasrais trisāhasraiḥ prabhadrakaiḥ vṛtaḥ śikhaṇḍī tvarito rājānaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayāt
english: Then, surrounded by a thousand chariots, three hundred elephants, five thousand horse, and three thousand Prabhadrakas, Śikhaṇḍin followed swiftly behind the king.

sanskrit: tato bherīḥ samājaghnuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuś ca daṃśitāḥ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ
english: Then, clad in mail, the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, beat their kettledrums and blew their conches.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahābāhur vāsudevo dhanaṃjayam eṣa prayāti tvarito krodhāviṣṭo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ jighāṃsuḥ sūtaputrasya tasyopekṣā na yujyate
english: Then the mighty-armed Vāsudeva said to Dhanaṃjaya: "Here goes Yudhiṣṭhira in haste, possessed by wrath and bent on slaying the sūta's son; to neglect him would not be fitting."

sanskrit: evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ śīghram aśvān acodayat dūraṃ ca yātaṃ rājānam anvagacchaj janārdanaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Hṛṣīkeśa swiftly urged on the horses, and Janārdana followed after the king, who had gone far ahead.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā yāntaṃ sūtaputrajighāṃsayā śokopahatasaṃkalpaṃ dahyamānam ivāgninā abhigamyābravīd vyāso dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Seeing him rushing on in his desire to slay the sūta's son, his resolve broken by grief and as if burning with fire, Vyāsa came up and spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma:

sanskrit: karṇam āsādya saṃgrāme diṣṭyā jīvati phalgunaḥ savyasācivadhākāṅkṣī śaktiṃ rakṣitavān hi saḥ
english: "By good fortune Phalguna lives, though he met Karṇa in battle; for that one, longing to slay Savyasācin, kept his lance in reserve."

sanskrit: na cāgād dvairathaṃ jiṣṇur diṣṭyā taṃ bharatarṣabha sṛjetāṃ spardhināv etau divyāny astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: "And by good fortune, O bull of the Bharatas, the victorious one did not come to single combat with him; for these two rivals would have loosed against each other their celestial weapons in every kind."

sanskrit: vadhyamāneṣu cāstreṣu pīḍitaḥ sūtanandanaḥ vāsavīṃ samare śaktiṃ dhruvaṃ muñced yudhiṣṭhira
english: "And as his weapons were struck down and the son of the sūta was hard pressed, he would surely have hurled in battle the lance of Vāsava, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: tato bhavet te vyasanaṃ ghoraṃ bharatasattama diṣṭyā rakṣo hataṃ yuddhe sūtaputreṇa mānada
english: "Then a dreadful calamity would have befallen you, O best of the Bharatas; by good fortune it was the rākṣasa who was slain in the fight by the sūta's son, O bestower of honour."

sanskrit: vāsavīṃ kāraṇaṃ kṛtvā kālenāpahato hy asau tavaiva kāraṇād rakṣo nihataṃ tāta saṃyuge
english: "Making the lance of Vāsava the occasion, he was carried off by Time; for your sake, my son, was the rākṣasa slain in battle."

sanskrit: mā krudho bharataśreṣṭha mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ prāṇinām iha sarveṣām eṣā niṣṭhā yudhiṣṭhira
english: "Be not wrathful, O best of the Bharatas, nor set your mind upon grief; this is the end of all living beings here, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ pārthivaiś ca mahātmabhiḥ kauravān samare rājann abhiyudhyasva bhārata pañcame divase caiva pṛthivī te bhaviṣyati
english: "Together with all your brothers and the great-souled kings, do battle against the Kauravas, O king, O Bhārata; and on the fifth day the earth shall be yours."

sanskrit: nityaṃ ca puruṣavyāghra dharmam eva vicintaya ānṛśaṃsyaṃ tapo dānaṃ kṣamāṃ satyaṃ ca pāṇḍava
english: "And ever, O tiger among men, dwell upon righteousness alone — upon mercy, austerity, charity, forbearance, and truth, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: sevethāḥ paramaprīto yato dharmas tato jayaḥ ity uktvā pāṇḍavaṃ vyāsas tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: "Cherish these with the highest delight; where dharma is, there is victory." Having so spoken to the Pāṇḍava, Vyāsa vanished then and there.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ghaṭotkace tu nihate sūtaputreṇa tāṃ niśām duḥkhāmarṣavaśaṃ prāpto dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When Ghaṭotkaca had been slain by the sūta's son that night, the son of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, fell under the sway of grief and indignation.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭva bhīmena mahatīṃ vāryamāṇāṃ camūṃ tava dhṛṣṭadyumnam uvācedaṃ kumbhayoniṃ nivāraya
english: Seeing your mighty host held back by Bhīma, he said this to Dhṛṣṭadyumna: "Hold off the pitcher-born one."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi droṇavināśāya samutpanno hutāśanāt saśaraḥ kavacī khaḍgī dhanvī ca paratāpanaḥ abhidrava raṇe hṛṣṭo na ca te bhīḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "For you were born from the fire for the destruction of Droṇa, armed with arrows, mailed, sword-bearing, bow-wielding, a scorcher of foes; charge joyfully into battle, and let there be no fear in you at all."

sanskrit: janamejayaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca daurmukhiś ca yaśodhanaḥ abhidravantu saṃhṛṣṭāḥ kumbhayoniṃ samantataḥ
english: "Let Janamejaya and Śikhaṇḍin and Daurmukhi, rich in glory, charge in their joy upon the pitcher-born one from every side."

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca draupadeyāḥ prabhadrakāḥ drupadaś ca virāṭaś ca putrabhrātṛsamanvitau
english: "Let Nakula and Sahadeva, the sons of Draupadī, the Prabhadrakas, and Drupada and Virāṭa, attended by their sons and brothers,"

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ kekayāś caiva pāṇḍavaś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ abhidravantu vegena bhāradvājavadhepsayā
english: "and Sātyaki and the Kekayas, and the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya — let them charge with fury in their desire to slay the son of Bharadvāja."

sanskrit: tathaiva rathinaḥ sarve hastyaśvaṃ yac ca kiṃ cana pādātāś ca raṇe droṇaṃ prāpayantu mahāratham
english: "And likewise let all the chariot-warriors, every elephant and horse there is, and the foot-soldiers, bring the great chariot-warrior Droṇa to bay in battle."

sanskrit: tathājñaptās tu te sarve pāṇḍavena mahātmanā abhyadravanta vegena kumbhayoniṃ yuyutsayā
english: Thus commanded by the great-souled Pāṇḍava, they all charged with fury upon the pitcher-born one, eager for battle.

sanskrit: āgacchatas tān sahasā sarvodyogena pāṇḍavān pratijagrāha samare droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: As the Pāṇḍavas came on suddenly with all their effort, Droṇa, the best of weapon-bearers, received them in battle.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā sarvodyogena pāṇḍavān abhyadravat susaṃkruddha icchan droṇasya jīvitam
english: Then king Duryodhana, with all his effort, greatly enraged, charged upon the Pāṇḍavas, wishing to preserve Droṇa's life.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ śrāntavāhanasainikam pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca garjatām itaretaram
english: Then there broke out a battle of warriors and mounts grown weary, of Pāṇḍavas and Kurus roaring at one another.

sanskrit: nidrāndhās te mahārāja pariśrāntāś ca saṃyuge nābhyapadyanta samare kāṃ cic ceṣṭāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Blinded by sleep, O great king, and worn out in the fray, those great chariot-warriors could not summon up any exertion in the battle.

sanskrit: triyāmā rajanī caiṣā ghorarūpā bhayānakā sahasrayāmapratimā babhūva prāṇahāriṇī vadhyatāṃ ca tathā teṣāṃ kṣatānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
english: And that night of three watches, dreadful of aspect and terrifying, became like a night of a thousand watches, life-destroying, above all to those being slain and to the wounded.

sanskrit: aho rātriḥ samājajñe nidrāndhānāṃ viśeṣataḥ sarve hy āsan nirutsāhāḥ kṣatriyā dīnacetasaḥ tava caiva pareṣāṃ ca gatāstrā vigateṣavaḥ
english: Ah, what a night it grew to be, above all for those blinded by sleep! For all the warriors, yours and the foe's alike, were without spirit and downcast in heart, their weapons spent, their arrows gone.

sanskrit: te tathā pārayantaś ca hrīmantaś ca viśeṣataḥ svadharmam anupaśyanto na jahuḥ svām anīkinīm
english: Yet, enduring as they were and possessed of shame above all else, looking to their own duty, they did not forsake their own battle-line.

sanskrit: śastrāṇy anye samutsṛjya nidrāndhāḥ śerate janāḥ gajeṣv anye ratheṣv anye hayeṣv anye ca bhārata
english: Some men, casting away their weapons, lay blinded by sleep — some upon elephants, some upon chariots, and some upon horses, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nidrāndhā no bubudhire kāṃ cic ceṣṭāṃ narādhipāḥ te 'nyonyaṃ samare yodhāḥ preṣayanta yamakṣayam
english: Blinded by sleep, the chieftains were aware of no exertion at all; those warriors sent one another in battle to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: svapnāyamānās tv apare parān iti vicetasaḥ ātmānaṃ samare jaghnuḥ svān eva ca parān api
english: Others, sunk as in a dream and bereft of sense, took men for foes and in the battle struck down their own selves, their own people, and the enemy alike.

sanskrit: nānāvāco vimuñcanto nidrāndhās te mahāraṇe yoddhavyam iti tiṣṭhanto nidrāsaṃsaktalocanāḥ
english: Uttering all manner of cries, blinded by sleep in that great battle, they stood saying "We must fight," though their eyes were fast clinging with slumber.

sanskrit: saṃmardyānye raṇe ke cin nidrāndhāś ca parasparam jaghnuḥ śūrā raṇe rājaṃs tasmiṃs tamasi dāruṇe
english: Some heroes, crushing one another in the fray and blinded by sleep, struck one another down in the battle, O king, in that fearsome darkness.

sanskrit: hanyamānaṃ tathātmānaṃ parebhyo bahavo janāḥ nābhyajānanta samare nidrayā mohitā bhṛśam
english: Many men, sorely stupefied by sleep, did not even perceive in the battle that their own selves were being struck down by the foe.

sanskrit: teṣām etādṛśīṃ ceṣṭāṃ vijñāya puruṣarṣabhaḥ uvāca vākyaṃ bībhatsur uccaiḥ saṃnādayan diśaḥ
english: Perceiving such a plight among them, Bībhatsu, that bull among men, spoke aloud these words, making the quarters resound:

sanskrit: śrāntā bhavanto nidrāndhāḥ sarva eva savāhanāḥ tamasā cāvṛte sainye rajasā bahulena ca
english: "You are all weary and blinded by sleep, mounts and all, and the army is enveloped in darkness and in thick clouds of dust."

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ yadi manyadhvam upāramata sainikāḥ nimīlayata cātraiva raṇabhūmau muhūrtakam
english: "If you, O soldiers, think it good, then desist, and close your eyes here upon this very battlefield for a little while."

sanskrit: tato vinidrā viśrāntāś candramasy udite punaḥ saṃsādhayiṣyathānyonyaṃ svargāya kurupāṇḍavāḥ
english: "Then, sleep gone and rested, when the moon has risen again, you Kurus and Pāṇḍavas shall once more dispatch one another to heaven."

sanskrit: tad vacaḥ sarvadharmajñā dhārmikasya niśamya te arocayanta sainyāni tathā cānyonyam abruvan
english: Hearing that word of the righteous one, the armies, knowing every duty, found it good, and spoke thus to one another:

sanskrit: cukruśuḥ karṇa karṇeti rājan duryodhaneti ca upāramata pāṇḍūnāṃ viratā hi varūthinī
english: They cried out, "Karṇa, O Karṇa!" and, "O Duryodhana!" — "Desist! the host of the Pāṇḍavas has indeed left off the fight," O king.

sanskrit: tathā vikrośamānasya phalgunasya tatas tataḥ upāramata pāṇḍūnāṃ senā tava ca bhārata
english: And as Phalguna cried out thus on every side, the army of the Pāṇḍavas and yours too left off the battle, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tām asya vācaṃ devāś ca ṛṣayaś ca mahātmanaḥ sarvasainyāni cākṣudrāḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ pratyapūjayan
english: That word of the great-souled one the gods and the sages, and all the noble-hearted armies, applauded with delight.

sanskrit: tat saṃpūjya vaco 'krūraṃ sarvasainyāni bhārata muhūrtam asvapan rājañ śrāntāni bharatarṣabha
english: Honouring that gentle word, all the wearied armies slept for a little while, O king, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: sā tu saṃprāpya viśrāmaṃ dhvajinī tava bhārata sukham āptavatī vīram arjunaṃ pratyapūjayat
english: And your banner-host, O Bhārata, having gained its rest and won its ease, paid honour to the hero Arjuna.

sanskrit: tvayi vedās tathāstrāṇi tvayi buddhiparākramau dharmas tvayi mahābāho dayā bhūteṣu cānagha
english: "In you abide the Vedas and the weapons; in you both wisdom and valour; in you dwells dharma, O mighty-armed one, and compassion for all beings, O sinless one."

sanskrit: yac cāśvastās tavecchāmaḥ śarma pārtha tad astu te manasaś ca priyān arthān vīra kṣipram avāpnuhi
english: "And the well-being we, restored, wish for you, O Pārtha — may it be yours; and swiftly may you attain, O hero, the dear desires of your heart."
